grammar.explanation:
Most nouns make the plural with **-s**. One book, two books. One diet, two diets.

Some nouns add **-es**. Use **-es** after **-s**, **-ss**, **-sh**, **-ch**, **-x**, and **-z**. One bus, two buses.

If a noun ends in a consonant and **y**, change **y** to **-ies**. One city, two cities.

A vowel and **y** just add **-s**. One boy, two boys. One key, two keys.

Some nouns change **-f** or **-fe** to **-ves**. One knife, two knives.

Some plurals are **irregular**. One child, two children. One foot, two feet. One person, two people.

Some nouns are the same in the singular and plural. One sheep, two sheep. One fish, two fish.

Some nouns are always plural. Jeans, trousers, and glasses are always plural. We say: my jeans **are** new.
